answer: An identity must lock a bond of 300 tokens for 20 epochs and bind to one hardware credential, logged as a pulse in the registry. Forging N identities locks 300N tokens, all slashed 100 percent, and the attacker waits 20 epochs per name. Copying a credential ties every fake to one shared bond, so detection by independent jurors costs the attacker 300 tokens per identity and the whole ferrous island of stake at once.
